questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large labelled diagram of the mammalian skin. *(9 marks)*
What are the differences between the epidermis of the mammalian skin and that of a leaf? *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Epidermis of mammalian skin | Epidermis of a leaf |
|---|---|
| Made of **many layers** of cells (stratified). | Made of **one layer** of cells. |
| The outer layer is **dead, cornified and filled with keratin**. | All the cells are **living**; the outer wall is covered with a **waxy cuticle**. |
| Has a **Malpighian layer** of dividing cells that renews the epidermis. | No special dividing layer. |
| Cells contain **melanin** pigment (protects against ultraviolet light). | No melanin; cells are **transparent**, so light reaches the mesophyll. |
| Has **no guard cells or stomata**, but pores of sweat glands and hair follicles. | Has **stomata with guard cells** for gas exchange. |
| **Does not carry out photosynthesis** (no chloroplasts). | The guard cells contain chloroplasts (the other epidermal cells do not). |
| Has sweat glands, sebaceous glands and hairs. | Has no glands; may have small hairs but no sweat. |

questions.enonce_markdown: How is temperature regulation carried out in the mammalian skin during over heating? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
When the body temperature rises above normal (about 37 $^\circ$C), the **hypothalamus** (which detects the temperature of the blood, helped by the skin receptors) sends nerve impulses to the skin, which responds as follows.

1. **Sweating:** the **sweat glands produce more sweat**; the **evaporation** of sweat from the skin surface takes latent heat from the body, which **cools** it.
2. **Vasodilation:** the **arterioles in the dermis dilate**, more blood flows through the **skin capillaries near the surface**, and **more heat is lost by radiation, conduction and convection**; the skin looks red.
3. **Hairs lie flat:** the **erector pili muscles relax**, so the hairs lie flat and **trap less air**, which reduces insulation and allows heat to escape.
4. The **metabolic rate is reduced** and there is no shivering.

The body temperature falls back to normal (negative feedback).
